{"content":"1|# Provisioning audit — D-Bus first
2|
3|- Task: `provision-audit-20261018`, follow-up to OD-111.
4|- Reviewer: Hermes / GPT-6 Astra Pro, with independent read-only storage and identity-contract reviewers; findings below cross-checked by the parent.
5|- Evidence timestamp: 2026-10-18T19:25:38Z.
6|- Repository: `/srv/git/odbus-verified`, branch `restore/devuan-storage-20261013`, HEAD `051a20d056afba074e21d797aa34f8947c543c5a` plus existing shared working-tree changes.
7|- Request: audit the provisioning script; owner correction: “be sure using dbus first”. This is review, not authorization to provision, repair, change grants, build or deploy.
8|
9|## Verdict
10|
11|Do not treat `deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh` as a working end-to-end provisioner against the current deployed namespace. Its older identity flow has independent path, operation-receipt and adoption-plan incompatibilities. The newer partitioned-disk flow has guest-FUSE and upgrade-root lifecycle defects. Direct native control and grant edits also fall outside the canonical D-Bus admission/readback path.
12|
13|The two flows are deliberately different: the legacy identity mode expects an unpartitioned leaf and plan versions 2/3; the manual GPT/overlay path uses version 4. Version 4 and its `partitioned_overlay` field are recognized by the owner. Findings about one flow are not assertions that the other has the same defect. Later-phase legacy findings are latent behind its earlier failures, not observed live outages.
14|
15|## Findings
16|
17|### F1 — High: legacy operation calls use a removed receipt interface
18|
19|Location: `deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:331-343`, callers at `396-401`, `454-455`, `493-507`.
20|
21|`lungs_call` writes and closes `operations/<method>/call`, then looks for sibling `error` and `result` files. Current `crates/threetched-fs/src/namespace.rs:1027-1037` projects only `call`. The live `inspect_provision_preflight` directory likewise contains only `call`, `input.schema.json`, `metadata.json`, and `output.schema.json`.
22|
23|Terminal receipt/diagnostic bytes are per-open-handle (`fuse_fs.rs:600-623`), and the supported mounted client writes, fsyncs, seeks and reads the same descriptor (`mounted.rs:394-410`). Closing the wrapper's write-only descriptor discards its access to that receipt. Even after correcting paths, the initial inventory gate cannot consume the current interface.
24|
25|Every invocation is also on the left side of `||`; Bash's conditional-function errexit behavior means the internal `set -e` is not a substitute for explicit checks on the write and first `jq`. On an older mount with sibling receipt files, the wrapper additionally lacks request correlation and mount-continuity checks. That stale-receipt possibility is conditional, not a demonstrated exploit on the current mount.
26|
27|Repair direction: use the supported mounted `invoke` path, keep its same-handle terminal diagnostic, and preserve its contract/mount validation. Do not add a parallel backend client or restore global receipt files.
28|
29|### F2 — High: both adoption entry points select absent host paths
30|
31|Locations:
32|- `provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:290,324-328`: `/usr/local/bin/3tched-fs`, `/run/mount/3tchedFS`.
33|- `prepare-chatbot-adoption.sh:26-29`: `/opt/op-dbus/current/bin/3tched-fs`, `/run/mount/3tchedFS`.
34|
35|Read-only `stat` verified all three historical paths are absent on this host. The actual client is `/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs`; `findmnt` confirms `/run/mounts/3tchedFS` is mounted as `fuse.3tchedFS`.
36|
37|Effect: default legacy invocation stops before owner admission; the new preparation helper cannot issue its owner preflight. Fixing only the executable does not fix the mount or F1. Guest mount paths are a different contract and must not be globally renamed to match the host.
38|
39|### F3 — High: legacy plans contain a field the owner rejects
40|
41|Location: `provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:459-474`, especially `principal_group` at line 464.
42|
43|The digest-pinned plan is decoded as `CleanPlan`, which has `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and no `principal_group` field (`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/identity_clean_provision.rs:52-77,575`). A valid digest selects this decoder through `identity_seed_provision.rs:719-728`.
44|
45|Effect, once the earlier blockers are repaired: adoption rejects the wrapper's plan after the stopped native container, writable leaf and mounts have already been created. The intentionally retained candidate requires reconciliation; rerunning creation is not a repair.
46|
47|Repair direction: reconcile the author with the existing owner contract. Group policy is a separate authorization concern; do not silently expand the adoption schema merely to accept this field.
48|
49|### F4 — High: binding the new root deletes the guest's FUSE mount declaration
50|
51|Location: `deploy/scripts/bind-instance-root.sh:76-78`.
52|
53|The helper truncates the inherited `/etc/fstab` to two comments. Image preparation explicitly appends `3tchedfs.fstab` (`deploy/workspace-image/prepare-lungs-client.sh:57-63`), and the guest service calls `mount /run/mount/3tchedfs` with no source/options (`deploy/workspace-image/3tchedfs.service:7-11`), relying on that declaration.
54|
55|Trigger: documented initial provisioning with an empty upgrade layer, so the seed-root `/etc/fstab` is the effective guest file. Effect: guest FUSE cannot mount through its service even though the root-binding receipt sets `guest_fuse_configured=true` (`bind-instance-root.sh:91-95`). This is a source-to-source incompatibility; the current private guest filesystem was not inspected.
56|
57|Repair direction: preserve the intended FUSE declaration while removing only unsafe host/physical-storage mounts. A blanket fstab replacement is not sufficient.
58|
59|### F5 — High: normal upgrade synchronization returns success with the native root detached
60|
61|Location: `deploy/scripts/sync-instance-upgrade.sh:88-109,132-162`.
62|
63|Both `sync` and `boot` detach agent/persistence mounts, native root, merged view and lower-layer mounts before transfer. Both publish phase `paired`, but only `boot` rebuilds the mounts. Thus normal `--sync-upgrade` on a bound, stopped guest exits successfully with its root absent.
64|
65|Canonical start verifies the overlay and all sibling mounts (`identity_clean_provision/storage.rs:289-326`, `partitioned.rs:107-125`), so a later start cannot accept that state. `bind-instance-root.sh:15-16` is not an ordinary recovery path: it only admits `container-defined` with `root_bound=false`, not the already-bound receipt.
66|
67|Repair direction: define and implement complete post-sync restoration for an existing bound guest, retaining the no-live-lower-mutation rule. Publish completion only after mount/readback verification.
68|
69|### F6 — High, latent legacy phase: a selected group can invalidate grants for every principal
70|
71|Location: `provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:264-267,525-548`.
72|
73|The script accepts any name from its closed group list, but writes that name without verifying the group's definition exists in the actual policy document or validating the replacement document. `interceptor.rs:1818-1828` requires referenced groups to exist. An otherwise valid policy without the selected group becomes invalid after this edit.
74|
75|The materializer rejects the entire document, removes readiness and publishes `{}` (`src/bin/op-grants-materializer.rs:95-111`); runtime grant readers also validate the whole policy. Consequence: selecting a syntactically accepted but undefined group can remove effective access for unrelated principals once the materializer observes the replacement.
76|
77|No live grants were read or changed. This finding does not assert that any particular group is currently missing.
78|
79|### F7 — High, latent legacy phase: running/boot-enabled completion precedes grant publication
80|
81|Location: `provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:503-548`.
82|
83|The sequence is adoption, optional start via `touch_session`, active/native readback, `seed-enable-boot`, then checking and rewriting the grants file. Missing/unwritable policy, malformed JSON, absent `python3` (not in dependency precheck at 281), or F6 therefore happens after the guest can be running and boot-enabled under its old grants.
84|
85|Even a successful replacement is not followed by materialized-policy readback. `OP_CAPABILITY_GRANTS` selects the script's file independently of materializer `OP_GRANTS_SOURCE` and reader `OP_GRANTS_PATH` (`op-grants-materializer.rs:140-150`, `interceptor.rs:1845-1854`). Selecting a group also retains explicit principal capabilities through `setdefault` at line 536; it is not a complete privilege replacement.
86|
87|Repair direction: keep authorization changes separate and explicitly approved, validate and verify their effective state before depending on them, and do not publish full provisioning completion ahead of a required authorization step.
88|
89|### F8 — Medium/security, latent legacy phase: whole-policy replacement can undo another writer's revocation
90|
91|Location: `provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:530-544`.
92|
93|The script reads and atomically replaces the entire grant document, without a policy-wide writer lock or compare-and-swap. Its lock at 314-319 covers only this provisioning session. If another authorized writer changes an unrelated principal between the read and replacement, that update is lost; a concurrent revocation can be restored from stale input. Atomic rename prevents partial-file visibility, not lost updates. No post-write policy readback detects this.
94|
95|### F9 — Medium/control-plane: implemented native operations are invoked outside D-Bus admission
96|
97|Locations:
98|- `provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:227-245`: standalone image creation and start use direct Incus CLI.
99|- `bind-instance-root.sh:66-74`: native device removal/addition uses direct Incus CLI.
100|
101|Existing plugin implementations include image-based `create_instance`, `start_instance`, `add_device`, and `remove_device`, declared in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/incus.rs:2947-2998,3078-3102`; device changes perform ETag-conditioned native updates at 2855-2897. Canonical dispatch coordinates observation and commits full authoritative state (`incus_observer.rs:193-221`). Direct CLI calls skip that caller admission and coordinated publication path.
102|
103|For the requested D-Bus-first behavior, prefer the declared identity-bound methods wherever they cover the operation; preserve capability checks and stop on denial. This is a control-plane/audit-boundary violation, not proof of unprivileged escalation.
104|
105|Important exceptions: do not claim the generic method can already replace empty Incus creation (`image_source` requires an image, incus.rs:2355-2373), provider-owned `volatile.last_state.idmap` changes (`validate_config`, 2345-2350), or every storage/profile operation. These require explicit maintenance contracts, not invented plugin methods. Raw GPT creation, creation-only blank-leaf addition and host mount ownership remain assigned to the external provisioner. A generic Btrfs method's existence does not cancel that ownership rule.
106|
107|### F10 — Medium, conditional: chatbot GPT restoration suppresses other identities
108|
109|Location: `deploy/runit/identity-roots/run:33-38`.
110|
111|When the chatbot boot receipt exists, the service restores it, publishes global readiness and executes `sleep infinity`. The subsequent physical-identity loop and other legacy handling at 44-112 are unreachable.
112|
113|Trigger: this GPT chatbot coexists with another completed boot-enabled identity. Effect: the other root is not restored, while the shared identity-roots readiness signal is published. This audit did not establish that a second such identity currently exists.
114|
115|## Additional limitations, not claimed runtime incidents
116|
117|- Fresh-only version-4 preparation: `prepare-chatbot-adoption.sh:31-36` accepts only revision 0 / empty operation ID. The owner also supports an exact explicit-deletion tombstone (`identity_clean_provision.rs:294-363`). Preparing a partitioned replacement after supported deletion therefore lacks a matching helper path. Existing-plan refusal is deliberate fail-closed behavior, not itself a bug.
118|- Retention/recovery: every stopped `boot` performs a new transfer; snapshots and prior writable `@` copies are retained (`sync-instance-upgrade.sh:110-134`). Cleanup is explicitly documented as unfinished (`docs/src/operations/shared-seed-provisioning.md:54-58`). Capacity failure can leave detached views and `send-intent`, which ordinary reruns reject. No exhaustion or data loss was observed. Retention must follow the storage owner's policy; do not invent a global subvolume cap or delete history in this audit.
119|- `incus-ct-chatbot` is listed as retired; it was not treated as the active boot owner. The demonstrated GPT path is `identity-roots → restore-chatbot-root → sync-instance-upgrade boot`.

{"content":"1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# Invoke one plugin method through a mounted 3tchedFS namespace (write `call`, read
3|# `result` / `error`). The mount must already be bound to the caller's identity
4|# (e.g. /run/mounts/3tchedFS + /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock).
5|#
6|# Capability grants and op-grants-materializer are not exposed here; durable policy
7|# stays under /etc/opdbus/local/ with owner-approved deltas only.
8|#
9|# Usage:
10|#   deploy/scripts/3tchedfs-invoke.sh <plugin> <method> [json-args]
11|#   OP_3TCHEDFS_MOUNT=/run/mounts/3tchedFS deploy/scripts/3tchedfs-invoke.sh tched_router config_get '{"path":"agents.dashboard.model_provider"}'
12|set -euo pipefail
13|
14|die() { echo "3tchedfs-invoke: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
15|
16|MOUNT="${OP_3TCHEDFS_MOUNT:-/run/mounts/3tchedFS}"
17|PLUGIN="${1:?plugin id}"
18|METHOD="${2:?method name}"
19|shift 2
20|ARGS="${1:-'{}'}"
21|if [[ $# -gt 1 ]]; then
22|  die "pass json-args as one quoted argument"
23|fi
24|TIMEOUT_SEC="${OP_3TCHEDFS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT:-30}"
25|
26|[[ -f "$MOUNT/.3tchedfs.json" ]] || die "not a 3tchedFS root: $MOUNT"
27|case "$(findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T "$MOUNT" 2>/dev/null || true)" in
28|  fuse|fuse.3tchedFS) ;;
29|  *) die "namespace is not a fuse 3tchedFS mount: $MOUNT" ;;
30|esac
31|
32|OP="$MOUNT/plugins/$PLUGIN/operations/$METHOD"
33|[[ -d "$OP" ]] || die "operation absent: $PLUGIN/$METHOD"
34|[[ -f "$OP/input.schema.json" ]] || die "missing input schema: $OP"
35|
36|if ! printf '%s' "$ARGS" | jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
37|  die "json-args must be valid JSON"
38|fi
39|
40|# Clear stale receipt files and write fresh call
41|>"$OP/result" 2>/dev/null || true
42|>"$OP/error" 2>/dev/null || true
43|printf '%s' "$ARGS" >"$OP/call"
44|
45|deadline=$((SECONDS + TIMEOUT_SEC))
46|while ((SECONDS < deadline)); do
47|  if [[ -s "$OP/error" ]]; then
48|    cat "$OP/error" >&2
49|    exit 1
50|  fi
51|  if [[ -s "$OP/result" ]]; then
52|    jq . "$OP/result"
53|    exit 0
54|  fi
55|  sleep 0.2
56|done
57|

{"content":"1|#!/bin/sh
2|# activate-golden.sh — the one command for deploying a new version.
3|#
4|#   sudo ./activate-golden.sh
5|#
6|# Run it after the release build and seal:
7|#   CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release
8|#   sudo target/release/opblob seal-shm && sudo target/release/opblob persist
9|# OP_RELEASE_DIR selects one prepared optimized artifact directory for both
10|# release-controller verification and golden preparation (default target/release).
11|#
12|# What it does:
13|# 1. Native provision-slots reconciles any interrupted transaction and prepares
14|#    the owned golden/slot layout. Recovery-only work stops this invocation.
15|# 2. Prepares /opt/op-dbus/golden from target/release and the sealed catalog
16|#    (internal helper deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh; it never builds or seals).
17|# 3. Native release sends/receives the immutable generation into the inactive
18|#    slot, rotates read-only overlays at the inventory's owned host targets,
19|#    and restores affected consumers' wanted states. Only active + previous remain.
20|#
21|# Undo the last release:
22|#   sudo /usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch rollback
23|set -eu
24|PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
25|LC_ALL=C
26|export PATH LC_ALL
27|
28|REPO=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
29|OP_RELEASE_DIR=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_RELEASE_DIR:-"$REPO/target/release"}")
30|export OP_RELEASE_DIR
31|RELEASE_BASE=/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release
32|RELEASE_LAUNCH=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release-launch
33|RELEASE_BIN=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release
34|RELEASE_BOOT=/etc/init.d/op-release-activate
35|
36|[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: run as root (sudo ./activate-golden.sh)' >&2; exit 1; }
37|[ "$#" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: takes no arguments' >&2; exit 1; }
38|# Check the execution path before invoking any installed kit code. The launcher
39|# independently checks the complete approved manifest and kernel/BTF pair.
40|for directory in / /usr /usr/local /usr/local/libexec "$RELEASE_BASE" /etc /etc/init.d; do
41|    directory_mode=0$(stat -c %a "$directory")
42|    [ -d "$directory" ] && [ ! -L "$directory" ] &&
43|        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$directory")" = 0:0 ] &&
44|        [ "$((directory_mode & 07022))" -eq 0 ] ||
45|        { echo "activate-golden.sh: insecure release-kit directory: $directory" >&2; exit 1; }
46|done
47|for artifact in "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" "$RELEASE_BIN" "$RELEASE_BOOT"; do
48|    [ -f "$artifact" ] && [ ! -L "$artifact" ] &&
49|        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a:%h "$artifact")" = 0:0:755:1 ] ||
50|        { echo "activate-golden.sh: install the approved root-owned release kit: $artifact" >&2; exit 1; }
51|done
52|cmp -s "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" "$REPO/deploy/release/op-release-launch" &&
53|    cmp -s "$RELEASE_BIN" "$OP_RELEASE_DIR/op-release" &&
54|    cmp -s "$RELEASE_BOOT" "$REPO/deploy/release/op-release-activate" ||
55|    { echo 'activate-golden.sh: installed release kit differs from this build; refusing an old or mixed kit' >&2; exit 1; }
56|
57|"$RELEASE_LAUNCH" provision-slots
58|"$REPO/deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh"
59|exec "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" release","total_lines":59,"file_size":3008,"truncated":false,"is_binary":false,"is_image":false,"not_found":false}

{"content":"1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# Provision a fresh shared root for the EXISTING configured chatbot key.
3|# Completed manual storage stage (no identity/backend preflight):
4|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-disk 3tchedChatbot
5|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --inspect-disk 3tchedChatbot
6|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-container 3tchedChatbot
7|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
8|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --bind-root 3tchedChatbot
9|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-adoption 3tchedChatbot
10|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
11|#     [--root-gib 20 --upgrade-gib 40]   # prepare-disk only
12|# Creates /var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/NAME.img: raw GPT root + upgrade.
13|# --prepare-container defines the stopped chatbot and socket profile only;
14|# it does not bind the prepared root, adopt the identity or start the guest.
15|# This stage ends before formatting, seed attachment, Incus creation or Cozo
16|# registration. Existing identity mode below remains the older unpartitioned
17|# leaf workflow; do not pass a partitioned image to that mode.
18|# Usage:
19|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh LABEL --session-id UUID --pubkey B64 \
20|#     --operator-session UUID --leaf-path ABSOLUTE_PATH --principal-group '$ROOT' \
21|#     [--fstorage-gib N] [--no-start]
22|#     [--container-name 3tchedChatbot]   # configured chatbot key only
23|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh NAME --system \
24|#     [--image ALIAS|FINGERPRINT] [--storage POOL] [--no-start]
25|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --system NAME [system options]
26|#
27|# Identity mode never signs up an account, generates/copies credentials,
28|# deletes/recreates a container, or attaches a leaf to an Incus filesystem.
29|# Clean replacement is currently scoped to the configured chatbot alias
30|# 3tchedChatbot. LABEL is display metadata, never authority.
31|# Existing native names and storage receipts are refused.
32|# --no-start prepares storage, reconciles and verifies attach, leaving STOPPED.
33|# The old native instance must be stopped. The supported owner operation
34|# creates a fresh parked current-schema record using the same key and SID;
35|# supported touch then starts it after attached readback. --no-start leaves
36|# the new identity parked. Credential bytes are not requested or inspected;
37|# supported method results redact them. This wrapper never mints credentials.
38|# Completion enables root/FUSE restoration on boot; --no-start records a
39|# stopped boot policy. Incomplete storage never receives a boot-ready marker.
40|# The physical seed is one immutable filesystem shared by all leaves. Storage
41|# preparation uses its existing seven subvolumes through a private writable
42|# sprout; it never snapshots, copies, sends or receives a container root.
43|# Each guest gets its session ID as /etc/hostname and the LXC UTS hostname.
44|# seed-lungs configures the persistent Incus disk attaching the identity's own
45|# host FUSE mount at /run/mount/3tchedFS on every start.
46|# The 3tched-lungs profile provides /run tmpfs and the dedicated host socket
47|# directory at the same /run/opdbus/lungs path inside each new container.
48|# Failures retain native/storage intent and private sanitized receipts.
49|# Host helper/catalog defaults select activated release artifacts.
50|# Selected overrides must be root-controlled. This is host operator maintenance,
51|# not a guest-accessible host socket or a new identity minting authority.
52|# --system remains ordinary Raccoon cloud provisioning without identity changes.
53|set -euo pipefail
54|die() { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
55|need_cmd() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "missing command: $1"; }
56|usage() { sed -n '2,20p' "$0"; }
57|if [[ $# == 0 || ${1:-} == -h || ${1:-} == --help ]]; then usage; exit 0; fi
58|prepare_chatbot_container() (
59|    # Host preparation only: no identity adoption, root copy, device-add or start.
60|    [[ $# == 1 && $1 == 3tchedChatbot ]] || die 'usage: --prepare-container 3tchedChatbot'
61|    [[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || die 'container preparation requires host root'
62|    for tool in incus jq findmnt stat flock realpath sync; do need_cmd "$tool"; done
63|    incus() { command incus --force-local "$@"; }
64|    umask 077
65|    pool_root=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
66|    receipt=$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.json
67|    container_receipt=$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.incus.json
68|    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool_root" -o FSROOT) == /@3tched-leaf-pool &&
69|       -f $receipt && ! -L $receipt && ! -e $container_receipt && ! -L $container_receipt ]] ||
70|        die 'prepared disk receipt required; existing container intents must be reconciled manually'
71|    jq -e --arg name "$1" '.name==$name and .phase=="filesystems-prepared" and
72|        .layout=="raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1" and .filesystem_prepared==true and .identity_registered==false' \
73|        "$receipt" >/dev/null || die 'disk is not ready for container definition'
74|    image=$(jq -er .image "$receipt")
75|    [[ $image == "$pool_root/$1.img" && -f $image && ! -L $image &&
76|       $(stat -c %i "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_inode "$receipt")" &&
77|       $(stat -c %s "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$receipt")" ]] || die 'prepared image changed'
78|    exec 9>"$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.lock"
79|    flock -n 9 || die 'instance preparation active'
80|    instances=$(incus list -f json)
81|    jq -e --arg name "$1" 'type=="array" and all(.[]; .name!=$name)' <<<"$instances" >/dev/null ||
82|        die 'container already exists; never recreate it'
83|    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M /var/lib/incus-storage -o FSROOT) == /@incus ]] || die 'Incus subvolume not mounted'
84|    pool_source=/var/lib/incus-storage/identity-roots
85|    pools=$(incus storage list -f json)
86|    if jq -e 'any(.[]; .name=="identity-roots")' <<<"$pools" >/dev/null; then
87|        pool_json=$(incus query /1.0/storage-pools/identity-roots)
88|        jq -e --arg source "$pool_source" '.driver=="dir" and .status=="Created" and .config.source==$source' \
89|            <<<"$pool_json" >/dev/null || die 'identity-roots pool differs'
90|    else
91|        [[ ! -e /var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots &&
92|           ! -L /var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots &&
93|           ! -e $pool_source && ! -L $pool_source ]] || die 'retained pool paths require manual reconciliation'
94|        mkdir -m 0711 "$pool_source"
95|        incus storage create identity-roots dir "source=$pool_source"
96|    fi
97|    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/op-identity-root seed-profile
98|    sid=b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28
99|    public_key=[REDACTED:opaque-base64]
100|    jq -n --arg name "$1" --arg sid "$sid" --arg source "$pool_source" \
101|        '{version:1,phase:"container-create-intent",name:$name,session_id:$sid,pool_source:$source,
102|          identity_registered:false,root_bound:false,started:false}' > "$container_receipt"
103|    sync -f "$container_receipt"
104|    deny_policy=$(printf '%s\n' \
105|        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x4008941a,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]' \
106|        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x5000940f,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]' \
107|        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x5000943f,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]')
108|    incus init --empty "$1" --storage identity-roots --profile 3tched-lungs \
109|        --config security.privileged=false --config security.nesting=false \
110|        --config security.protection.shift=true --config boot.autostart=false \
111|        --config security.syscalls.deny_default=true --config "security.syscalls.deny=$deny_policy" \
112|        --config "user.opdbus.session_id=$sid" --config "user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key=$public_key" \
113|        --config user.display_name=control-plane-chatbot --config "raw.lxc=lxc.uts.name = $sid" </dev/null
114|    # Preserve the shared profile. Its historical initial.mode key is absent
115|    # from the sealed disk-device contract and /run already exists as 0755.
116|    incus config device override "$1" runtime-run
117|    incus config device unset "$1" runtime-run initial.mode
118|    instance=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$1")
119|    jq -e --arg name "$1" --arg sid "$sid" '.name==$name and .status=="Stopped" and
120|        .config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid' <<<"$instance" >/dev/null || die 'stopped definition readback differs'
121|    jq --argjson instance "$instance" '.phase="container-defined"|.instance=$instance' \
122|        "$container_receipt" > "$container_receipt.new"
123|    sync -f "$container_receipt.new"
124|    mv -T "$container_receipt.new" "$container_receipt"
125|    sync -f "$pool_root/.provisioning"
126|    printf 'Stopped container defined; root binding and identity adoption remain pending.\n'
127|)
128|case $1 in
129|    --prepare-adoption)
130|        shift
131|        script_dir=$(dirname -- "$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
132|        adoption_helper=$script_dir/prepare-chatbot-adoption.sh
133|        [[ -x $adoption_helper ]] || adoption_helper=$script_dir/prepare-chatbot-adoption
134|        [[ -x $adoption_helper ]] || die 'adoption plan helper missing'
135|        exec "$adoption_helper" "$@"
136|        ;;
137|    --bind-root)
138|        shift
139|        script_dir=$(dirname -- "$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
140|        bind_helper=$script_dir/bind-instance-root.sh
141|        [[ -x $bind_helper ]] || bind_helper=$script_dir/bind-instance-root
142|        [[ -x $bind_helper ]] || die 'root binding helper missing'
143|        exec "$bind_helper" "$@"
144|        ;;
145|    --prepare-container)
146|        shift
147|        prepare_chatbot_container "$@"
148|        exit
149|        ;;
150|    --pair-upgrade|--sync-upgrade|--upgrade-boot)
151|        upgrade_action=pair
152|        [[ $1 != --sync-upgrade ]] || upgrade_action=sync
153|        [[ $1 != --upgrade-boot ]] || upgrade_action=boot

12|    i=0

14|        i=$((i + 1))
15|        [ "$i" -ge 90 ] && { echo "dependency $1 not ready after 90s" >&2; exit 1; }
16|        sleep 1
17|    done

19|

21|
22|i=0

24|    i=$((i + 1))

32|helper=/usr/local/libexec/3tched/op-identity-root
33|gpt=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/.provisioning/3tchedChatbot.boot.json

35|    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/restore-chatbot-root || exit 1
36|    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal identity-roots

40|legacy=${IDENTITIES:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/identities}
41|physical_present=0
42|seed_readonly_ready=0
43|failed=0
44|for receipt in "$physical"/*/state.json; do
45|    [ -e "$receipt" ] || [ -L "$receipt" ] || continue
46|    physical_present=1
47|    name=$(basename "$(dirname "$receipt")")
48|    if [ "$name" != 3tchedChatbot ] && ! printf '%s' "$name" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
49|        echo "physical seed staging receipt $name: boot disabled"
50|        continue
51|    fi
52|    marker="$physical/$name/boot-ready.json"
53|    if [ ! -e "$marker" ] && [ ! -L "$marker" ]; then
54|        echo "physical seed $name: no authoritative-completion boot opt-in; skipped"
55|        continue
56|    fi
57|    # A canonical name alone does not prove provisioning completed. The helper
58|    # checks the owner attestation marker and all storage/native identity pins.
59|    if ! jq -e --arg name "$name" '
60|        .name == $name and .phase == "ready" and
61|        (.session == $name or ($name == "3tchedChatbot" and .session == "b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28"))
62|    ' "$receipt" >/dev/null; then
63|        echo "physical seed $name: invalid/incomplete receipt; legacy suppressed" >&2
64|        failed=$((failed + 1))
65|        continue
66|    fi
67|    start_on_boot=$(jq -er '.start_on_boot | select(type == "boolean") | tostring' "$marker") || {
68|        echo "physical seed $name: invalid boot completion policy" >&2
69|        failed=$((failed + 1))
70|        continue
71|    }
72|    # The physical partition's kernel RO flag is volatile across reboot.
73|    # The host owner restores it once, after ready/opt-in selection and before
74|    # any seed-check/up; verification failures stop boot restoration closed.
75|    if [ "$seed_readonly_ready" -eq 0 ]; then
76|        "$helper" seed-readonly || { echo "physical seed read-only enforcement failed" >&2; exit 1; }
77|        seed_readonly_ready=1
78|    fi
79|    state=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name/state" | jq -er '.status') || state=unknown
80|    case "$state" in
81|        Running)
82|            if "$helper" seed-check "$name"; then

84|            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
85|            ;;
86|        Stopped)

89|                else echo "physical seed $name: storage restored; boot start disabled"; fi
90|            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
91|            ;;
92|        *) echo "physical seed $name: unsupported native status $state" >&2
93|            failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
94|    esac
95|done

{"content":"1|#!/bin/sh
2|set -eu
3|
4|SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
5|PROVISIONER=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh
6|TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/provision-system-test.XXXXXX")
7|trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_ROOT"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
8|BIN="$TMP_ROOT/bin"
9|mkdir -p "$BIN"
10|
11|cat > "$BIN/incus" <<'STUB'
12|#!/bin/sh
13|printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$INCUS_LOG"
14|case "$1" in
15|    query)
16|        [ "${QUERY_FAIL:-0}" = 0 ] || exit 17
17|        if [ "${QUERY_MALFORMED:-0}" != 0 ]; then
18|            printf '{"metadata":[]}\n'
19|            exit 0
20|        fi
21|        if [ "${EXISTING_INSTANCE:-}" != "" ]; then
22|            printf '[{"name":"%s"}]\n' "$EXISTING_INSTANCE"
23|        else
24|            printf '[]\n'
25|        fi
26|        ;;
27|    init)
28|        [ "${INIT_FAIL:-0}" = 0 ] || exit 18
29|        [ "${CONFIG_FAIL:-0}" = 0 ] || exit 19
30|        ;;
31|    start) [ "${START_FAIL:-0}" = 0 ] ;;
32|esac
33|STUB
34|chmod +x "$BIN/incus"
35|for forbidden in wg busctl btrfs losetup zcall; do
36|    cat > "$BIN/$forbidden" <<'STUB'
37|#!/bin/sh
38|printf '%s %s\n' "${0##*/}" "$*" >> "$FORBIDDEN_LOG"
39|exit 99
40|STUB
41|    chmod +x "$BIN/$forbidden"
42|done
43|
44|fail() { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
45|run() {
46|    : > "$INCUS_LOG"
47|    if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" OPDBUS_IDENTITY_ROOT="$TMP_ROOT/identity-must-not-exist" "$@"; then
48|        return 0
49|    else
50|        return $?
51|    fi
52|}
53|assert_log() { grep -F -- "$1" "$INCUS_LOG" >/dev/null || fail "missing Incus call: $1"; }
54|assert_no_log() { ! grep -E -- "$1" "$INCUS_LOG" >/dev/null || fail "unexpected Incus call matching: $1"; }
55|INCUS_LOG="$TMP_ROOT/incus.log"
56|export INCUS_LOG
57|FORBIDDEN_LOG="$TMP_ROOT/forbidden.log"
58|export FORBIDDEN_LOG
59|
60|# Both accepted argument orders, explicit regular image/pool defaults, and ordinary start.
61|run "$PROVISIONER" app-api --system
62|assert_log 'query /1.0/instances?recursion=1'
63|assert_log 'init raccoon app-api --storage 3tched-storage --no-profiles'
64|assert_log '--config security.privileged=false --config security.nesting=false --config boot.autostart=false'
65|assert_log 'start app-api'
66|assert_no_log '(^| )(profile|device|delete|stop)( |$)'
67|
68|run "$PROVISIONER" --system queue-worker --image local:noble-system --storage custom-pool --no-start
69|assert_log 'init local:noble-system queue-worker --storage custom-pool --no-profiles'
70|assert_no_log '^start '
71|
72|# An explicit image equal to the identity default is still an explicit override.
73|run "$PROVISIONER" app-gateway --system --image 3a639373bb7a --no-start
74|assert_log 'init 3a639373bb7a app-gateway --storage 3tched-storage --no-profiles'
75|assert_no_log '^start '
76|
77|# Environment defaults select the regular system image and system storage pool.
78|: > "$INCUS_LOG"
79|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" SYSTEM_CONTAINER_IMAGE=images:ubuntu/noble SYSTEM_STORAGE_POOL=system-pool \
80|    "$PROVISIONER" --system worker-env --no-start; then
81|    :
82|else
83|    fail 'environment image/storage defaults failed'
84|fi
85|assert_log 'init images:ubuntu/noble worker-env --storage system-pool --no-profiles'
86|
87|# Exact existing instance is refused before any mutation.
88|: > "$INCUS_LOG"
89|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" EXISTING_INSTANCE=app-api "$PROVISIONER" app-api --system; then
90|    fail 'existing instance was accepted'
91|fi
92|assert_no_log '^(init|config|start|delete|stop) '
93|
94|# Identity-only switches are rejected before making any Incus call.
95|for option in --pubkey --identity-dir --private-key-file --email --mesh-ip --fstorage-gib --session-id; do
96|    : > "$INCUS_LOG"
97|    if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" "$PROVISIONER" app-api --system "$option" ignored; then
98|        fail "identity-only option accepted in system mode: $option"
99|    fi
100|    [ ! -s "$INCUS_LOG" ] || fail "Incus called for rejected identity-only option: $option"
101|done
102|for option in --ghostbridge --semantic --recreate; do
103|    : > "$INCUS_LOG"
104|    if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" "$PROVISIONER" app-api --system "$option"; then
105|        fail "identity-only option accepted in system mode: $option"
106|    fi
107|    [ ! -s "$INCUS_LOG" ] || fail "Incus called for rejected identity-only option: $option"
108|done
109|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" "$PROVISIONER" app-api --storage custom-pool; then
110|    fail '--storage without --system was accepted'
111|fi
112|
113|# Input validation and every Incus failure boundary propagate without later mutations.
114|for name in '-bad' 'bad/name' 'bad_name' 'trailing-' ''; do
115|    if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" "$PROVISIONER" --system "$name"; then
116|        fail "invalid name accepted: $name"
117|    fi
118|done
119|: > "$INCUS_LOG"
120|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" "$PROVISIONER" --system bad-image --image --invalid; then
121|    fail 'option-prefixed image was accepted'
122|fi
123|[ ! -s "$INCUS_LOG" ] || fail 'Incus called for rejected option-prefixed image'
124|: > "$INCUS_LOG"
125|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" QUERY_FAIL=1 "$PROVISIONER" --system query-fail; then fail 'query failure swallowed'; fi
126|assert_no_log '^(init|config|start) '
127|: > "$INCUS_LOG"
128|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" QUERY_MALFORMED=1 "$PROVISIONER" --system malformed-inventory; then
129|    fail 'malformed Incus inventory was accepted'
130|fi
131|assert_no_log '^(init|config|start) '
132|: > "$INCUS_LOG"
133|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" INIT_FAIL=1 "$PROVISIONER" --system init-fail; then fail 'init failure swallowed'; fi
134|assert_no_log '^(config|start) '
135|: > "$INCUS_LOG"
136|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" CONFIG_FAIL=1 "$PROVISIONER" --system config-fail; then fail 'config failure swallowed'; fi
137|assert_no_log '^start '
138|: > "$INCUS_LOG"
139|if PATH="$BIN:/usr/bin:/bin" INCUS_LOG="$INCUS_LOG" START_FAIL=1 "$PROVISIONER" --system start-fail; then fail 'start failure swallowed'; fi
140|
141|[ ! -e "$TMP_ROOT/identity-must-not-exist" ] || fail 'system mode created identity storage'
142|[ ! -s "$FORBIDDEN_LOG" ] || fail 'system mode invoked an identity/storage/Cozo helper'
143|printf 'PASS: standalone --system provisioning branch\n'","total_lines":143,"file_size":6069,"truncated":false,"is_binary":false,"is_image":false,"not_found":false}

{"content":"1|# Shared physical seed and private leaves
2|
3|## Manual provisioning checkpoint: partitioned instance disk
4|
5|The October 11 manual workflow uses a sparse QEMU raw image under
6|`/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool`, mounted from `@3tched-leaf-pool` on the host's
7|main Btrfs pool. This subvolume isolates the storage path, but shares that
8|pool's capacity. The shared seed remains the separate sealed 20 GiB partition;
9|no instance identity or Cozo binding is written into it.
10|
11|The completed image preparation step is available through the provisioner:
12|
13|```sh
14|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-disk 3tchedChatbot
15|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --inspect-disk 3tchedChatbot
16|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-filesystems 3tchedChatbot \
17|  --seed-device /dev/disk/by-uuid/3415d575-7224-4484-9e0d-06854ac5f032
18|```
19|
20|Preparation creates a 60 GiB sparse raw image with GPT: 20 GiB root and the
21|remaining approximately 40 GiB upgrade partition. `--root-gib` and
22|`--upgrade-gib` select capacities on a new image. The upgrade remainder is
23|slightly smaller than its requested capacity because GPT and alignment consume
24|space. The image and a private preparation receipt live in the leaf pool;
25|the receipt pins the image inode and both partition identities. An interrupted
26|creation retains its intent and image instead of retrying or cleaning them up.
27|`inspect` does not register or adopt an existing image.
28|
29|The filesystem stage attaches a read-only loop view of the sealed seed and adds
30|the blank root partition once as its writable leaf. It inherits the seven seed
31|subvolumes; it does not copy the root or create replacement agent subvolumes.
32|Only the upgrade partition is formatted, with one `@` subvolume. Shared and soul
33|are read-only in the leaf; memory, rules, skills and user are writable. Private
34|persistence directories are ordinary directories. Both mounts stay attached for
35|the next manual step. The receipt records loops, mounts and fresh filesystem
36|UUIDs. Interrupted intents require investigation, and prepared receipts cannot
37|repeat device-add or formatting. Never modify the seed after leaves depend on it.
38|
39|Neither stage performs seed transport, Incus creation, identity registration or
40|startup. They have no identity/backend preflight dependency.
41|Those later steps remain subject to the owner's manual
42|script comparison. The existing identity mode described below expects an
43|unpartitioned leaf and must not be used with this new partitioned image.
44|
45|The upgrade lifecycle is host → container only, using Btrfs without Unison:
46|
47|```sh
48|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
49|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
50|```
51|
52|Pairing sends a read-only snapshot of host upgrade `/dev/sdc3` (`@`) to
53|partition 2 during provisioning, including when the first upgrade is empty.
54|Subsequent synchronization sends incrementally from the retained
55|common baseline, including deletions within the upgrade tree. Received baselines stay read-only;
56|the published upgrade `@` is a writable clone. Transfer intents and prior
57|versions are retained for recovery; interrupted publication is not retried
58|automatically. Snapshot retention cleanup is not implemented by this stage.
59|
60|The chatbot runit startup invokes `boot` for explicitly paired storage before
61|starting the container. It restores existing loop/mount attachments, synchronizes,
62|then publishes a read-only OverlayFS OS view at `.mounts/NAME/root-view`.
63|The upgrade layer takes precedence over the seed-root layer; an empty upgrade
64|uses the installed seed. Patches removing seed files must include OverlayFS
65|whiteouts: deleting a file from the upgrade tree alone reveals its seed copy.
66|The Btrfs layers receive the container UID mapping before mounting OverlayFS,
67|because this kernel rejects mapping the merged overlay. The view is bound at
68|the Incus-managed `identity-roots` rootfs, preserving its pool definition.
69|Six agent subvolumes are separately bound into `/agent`; their existing writable
70|or read-only policies remain in effect, with private persistence bound separately.
71|User contents are never sent or received. Synchronization detaches stopped OS
72|views before rotating a lower layer; it never changes Btrfs membership.
73|This new image is not yet admitted by the older unpartitioned root-owner lifecycle;
74|its identity-root integration remains part of the subsequent provisioning step.
75|
76|The seed has the seven sibling subvolumes and guest systemd FUSE service.
77|`@agent_rules/rules/rules.md` and `@agent_user/user/user.md` are initial
78|per-instance documents: their content is changed in each private writable leaf,
79|not in the sealed seed. Shared owner links expose cognitive memory, skills,
80|routing and plugins without granting authority or starting those features.
81|
82|## Earlier unpartitioned-leaf integration
83|
84|The following describes the earlier helper contract. Its device paths,
85|host-owned FUSE attachment and early backend gates are not the new manual
86|partitioned-disk workflow and still require reconciliation before automation.
87|
88|Identity provisioning uses one immutable Btrfs seed on the physical partition
89|currently named `/dev/sdb2`. Each container has its own writable leaf. A leaf
90|stores that container's changes; it does not contain a copied root filesystem.

92|after release activation, the operator entrypoint is

94|

97|uses these existing subvolumes in the sprout. It does not create snapshots,
98|send/receive root filesystems, copy seed images, or use an overlay root.
99|Readonly loop views reference the same physical partition bytes.
100|

103|and provisioning preflight operations through their `call` files. It checks
104|the operation receipts before invoking the read-only

106|an empty Incus instance with the `3tched-lungs` profile.

108|state, and refuses a direct mount of the physical source. The wrapper holds
109|a per-session lock; the helper serializes seed loop setup and leaf creation.
110|`seed-create` adds the new private writable leaf once. Later starts mount
111|that existing leaf; stopping does not remove a Btrfs member. Failed starts
112|also retain membership. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage;
113|its `attached` field describes logical attachment, not device membership.
114|The session hostname and private persistence are
115|created through the sprout, so those writes belong to the leaf. Persistence is
116|an ordinary mode-0700 directory at `@agent_user/persist`, bound to the guest's
117|`/opt/run-mounts/persist`. Provisioning creates no subvolumes at all: only the
118|seven inherited members are used. Agent soul,
119|and shared subvolumes remain protected in the guest view. Rules and user
120|preferences are instance-specific and writable in each private leaf.
121|
122|Storage receipts identify this layout as `shared-partition-siblings-v2` and
123|pin its inherited subvolume identities plus the persistence directory's inode,
124|parent subvolume identity, sprout FSID and image metadata digest. The directory must remain on its
125|parent filesystem and cannot be a symlink, separate mount, or subvolume.
126|Older v1 receipts with an extra `@persist` subvolume and snapshot-based receipts are
127|rejected; this change does not silently migrate them or replace existing
128|container roots. Existing live persistence and older containers are neither
129|deleted nor converted; replacement must be prepared separately. Historical
130|soul reconciliation now verifies existing subvolumes and native devices only,
131|and fails when they are missing instead of creating them.
132|
133|Before sealing a new base, `op-identity-image prepare TOP RELEASE_ID

135|critical file hashes and exact seven-member layout. It also prepares ordinary
136|mountpoint directories under `@/run/mount/3tchedFS` and `@/run/opdbus/lungs`.
137|The helper does not download or verify the archive signature, mount storage,
138|toggle SEEDING, format devices or create subvolumes. See
139|[image preparation](../../../deploy/workspace-image/README.md) for its input
140|contract. Creation fully verifies the pristine image before adding a leaf;
141|later checks verify the pinned metadata without rejecting legitimate private
142|package updates in the leaf.
143|
144|FUSE runs on the host. Fresh provisioning selects a persistent Incus `disk`
145|device named `3tched`, exposing the session's own host FUSE mount at
146|`/run/mount/3tchedFS`. The seed needs an empty destination directory, not a
147|guest FUSE daemon. A native instance UUID pins the host source and process
148|receipt. An existing legacy hook receipt is verified without silently
149|converting its attachment mechanism. The common `/etc/3tched` directories
150|are a separate read-only Incus disk attachment, with links from the inherited
151|agent subvolumes.
152|
153|The `3tched-lungs` Incus profile supplies these inherited devices:
154|
155|```yaml
156|config: {}
157|devices:
158|  runtime-run:
159|    type: disk
160|    source: "tmpfs:"
161|    path: /run
162|    initial.mode: "0755"
163|  lungs-socket-dir:
164|    type: disk
165|    source: /run/opdbus/lungs
166|    path: /run/opdbus/lungs
167|    readonly: "true"
168|```
169|
170|The bridge service creates its existing shared socket at
171|`/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock`. Mounting its dedicated parent directory keeps
172|socket replacement visible to each guest without exposing other host runtime
173|files. `seed-profile` creates this exact profile if absent and rejects existing
174|configuration drift. Provisioning also verifies the inherited devices and
175|rejects local overrides. The `/run` tmpfs is mounted before its child devices;
176|image directories alone would not establish that boot ordering.
177|
178|The bridge creates a root-owned socket with mode 0666 beneath the root-owned
179|0755 directory. Connection permission allows negotiation; each operation still
180|requires an authenticated identity and its existing capability grant. Host
181|`Bind(session)` requires UID 0 in the bridge's own user and PID namespaces.
182|Guest `BindCurrentContainer()` takes no session argument: it pins the socket's
183|original process with SO_PEERPIDFD and derives identity from the exact running
184|native container. Process, native UUID and authoritative identity are checked
185|again for each call. No SID1 file is installed in the guest.
186|
187|Clean replacement is scoped to the configured chatbot key and service identity
188|`b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, using the provisioner's configured native

{"content":"1|# Network Operations
2|
3|This page describes **how networking is supposed to work on the current Artix/runit host**, and points at the live inventory when the tree and the machine disagree.
4|
5|For a dated, command-verified snapshot of interfaces, Incus devices, listeners, xray SNI, and mesh forwarders, see:
6|
7|**[Host socket & network topology (live)](host-socket-topology-live.md)**
8|
9|Re-verify that file against the host before topology-changing work (new proxies, prom/graf exposure, socket migrations).
10|
11|## Agent rules and owner decisions (moved from AGENTS.md, 2026-10-14)
12|
13|Read this section before any network, Xray, WARP, decoy, OVS or firewall work.
14|AGENTS.md now only points here.
15|
16|**Partial restoration (2026-10-16).** The native `decoy-admin-reverse-ssh`
17|runit service is restored on the Devuan host using the existing
18|`/home/jeremy/.ssh/decoy_key` and strict host-key checking. The decoy publishes
19|`10.0.0.1:2222` bound to `wg-opdbus`, forwarding to its loopback reverse endpoint;
20|the tunnel terminates at the host's loopback SSH listener. WireGuard terminates
21|only on the decoy, never on this host. A fresh authenticated reverse connection
22|returned `jeremy` on `3tched` and matched the host's authoritative ED25519 key.
23|The external WireGuard-client leg was not exercised from this session.
24|
25|The target layout is eth0 as OVS uplink, pub0 for public addressing (not
26|administrative SSH), two IPv4 addresses on `rtly-lungs` including 10.0.0.2,
27|and three service aliases on ovsbr0 for EMQX, OpenFlow and Qdrant. OVS packages
28|are installed, but no bridge/address/route ownership cutover has occurred.
29|NetworkManager remains active until a protected transfer; afterward it must
30|remain installed but disabled, for emergency recovery only.
31|
32|Owner requests stopping at the application-bridge prerequisite. The existing
33|uplink service waits for `opdbus-rundirs`, which requires `/usr/local/bin/opblob`
34|and a prepared persisted catalog; that executable is absent. This is an
35|application-catalog bootstrap dependency, not proof that the bridge daemon must
36|run to create OVS. Do not bypass it or claim the network cutover is deployed.
37|Public recovery SSH is still enabled: a proposed private-only cutover was
38|reverted when its rollback helper could not execute on the `noexec` `/run`
39|mount. Move forward only with an approved, functioning rollback mechanism.
40|
41|**Current status (2026-10-14).** The host moved from Artix to Devuan 6 (runit:
42|`/etc/sv/<svc>`, enabled via `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`). Only `eth0`
43|(`188.68.58.237/22`, DHCP) is up; OVS, Incus, Xray and WARP are not installed yet.
44|Owner decision: the network lives on the **base system**, not in a golden release,
45|installed on a new machine by a network preinstall script that pulls these
46|sources from git. The rest of this page, including the GRE description below,
47|predates that move: GRE (`gre-decoy`) and `wgcf` were retired on 2026-10-04 (see
48|`deploy/runit/retired-services`), and `deploy/config/nftables.conf` says SSH
49|transport now uses `tun5`. Xray config/keys and the Xray Incus container are not
50|in git; the recovery disk keeps them under `received/271/root-271/`
51|(`etc/xray`, `var/lib/incus`, `etc/openvswitch`, `etc/nftables.conf`).
52|
53|**Network-critical services.** OVS, uplink, DHCP and the session bus require
54|deliberate operator action; a learning or inventory pass never restarts them.
55|
56|**Xray configuration policy — mandatory.** Xray's live config must exist only at
57|`/etc/xray/xray_config.json` inside the container. Never point Xray at
58|`/dev/shm/xray_config.json`, `/usr/local/etc/xray/config.json`, or any other
59|disk-backed live path. The static bootstrap config is materialized at boot; the
60|future model-generated generator replaces the same file atomically and reloads
61|through D-Bus. Models must not write or reload Xray directly.
62|
63|**Owner-confirmed network topology (2026-09-13).** There is no WireGuard on this
64|server. WireGuard terminates at the decoy; identity is transported by WARP.
65|WireGuard types, plugin declarations, credentials or historical configuration
66|paths in source do not establish a server WireGuard interface or a requirement to
67|install one. Classify those surfaces by their decoy/server role before proposing
68|implementation or retirement. An unwired `wgcf` method is not evidence that the
69|actual WARP identity transport is broken.
70|
71|**Owner decisions: decoy GRE, TLS and identity transport (2026-09-25; GRE since
72|retired).** The door stays `10.0.0.2:8090`: tonic with the internal `svc0`
73|certificate from the op-dbus local CA. The bridge no longer listens on
74|`127.0.0.1:8090` or `10.0.0.3:8090`, and it no longer serves a second browser
75|certificate. Browser-facing TLS terminates on the decoy at `10.0.0.1`. The decoy
76|mints the sealed identity blob, and WARP delivers it to the 8090 interceptor. The
77|oracle (OIA1) is the decoy's signed proof of the WireGuard peer, because
78|WireGuard exists only on the decoy. At the time, the decoy routed browser
79|traffic for `10.0.0.2` over `gre-host` with no WARP route in either main routing
80|table. The `gre-decoy` tunnel joined decoy and host: outer `188.68.58.237` ↔
81|`129.80.64.127`, inner `192.168.255.1/30` plus `10.0.0.2/32`, with `10.0.0.1` and
82|the WireGuard clients `10.0.0.5`–`10.0.0.7` routed via `192.168.255.2`. GRE
83|routing replaced NAT on that path: nftables is the firewall only, never a router,
84|so do not add DNAT, SNAT or masquerade for it. GRE is not encrypted, so anything
85|crossing it that is not TLS is readable on the path. MQTT stays on `10.0.0.3`,
86|aliased on `ovsbr0` beside the OpenFlow address `10.200.0.1`. Xray runs in its
87|container. op-web's page address is `http://10.0.0.4:8080`: plain HTTP outside
88|the TLS zone, with `10.0.0.4/32` on `gre-decoy` and routed from the decoy over
89|`gre-host`. The decoy issuer
90|(`/etc/systemd/system/op-decoy-issuer.service.d/browser-auth.conf` on the decoy,
91|not in this repo) hands out the IP door `https://10.0.0.2:8090` and allows the
92|`10.0.0.4` and `10.0.0.2` page origins; no domain name points browsers at the
93|decoy. Open on 2026-09-25: how the decoy-minted oracle reaches the interceptor
94|(the owner's direction then was over GRE). Until that lands, the deployed page
95|fetches OIA1 from `http://10.0.0.1:51888/identity/self`, and the door rejects a
96|request that carries no credential.
97|
98|## Model in one paragraph
99|
100|One OVS bridge (`ovsbr0`) carries the private fabric. Physical uplink (`eth0`) is enslaved and unaddressed; host L3 lives on OVS internal ports **`pub0`** (public) and **`svc0`** (`10.200.0.2/24`). The **xray** container is the only instance with a NIC on the bridge (`10.200.0.1`). WireGuard mesh interface **`3tched`** (`100.69.0.254/16`) is separate L3 and must never be routed via `ovsbr0`.
101|
102|**Shared socket fabric:** `op-grpc-bridge` dual-listens on host UDS `/run/opdbus/grpc.sock` and shared container UDS `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` (same gRPC routes). NIC-less containers bind-mount `/run/ghostbridge`. Some services still use Incus TCP proxies / mesh `fwd-*` (migration is incremental).
103|
104|**OpenFlow** (`op-of-controller` on `127.0.0.1:6653`) is intentionally NORMAL/standalone today — reserved for **future tag routing**, not a current blocker for the socket fabric.
105|
106|## Boot order (runit)
107|
108|```text
109|opdbus-rundirs
110|  → uplink-dhcp
111|  → ovsdb-server → ovs-vswitchd
112|  → ovsbr0-uplink → ovsbr0-addr → ovsbr0-svc-addr
113|  → op-of-controller
114|  → wg-3tched
115|  → op-grpc-bridge (cognitive in process) / op-web
116|```
117|
118|Config: `/etc/op-dbus/network.conf`  
119|Helpers: `/usr/local/libexec/3tched/*-up`
120|
121|## Public path
122|
123|Client DNS (NextDNS) → Oracle decoy → WireGuard mesh → host `fwd-8444` → xray SNI on `10.200.0.1:8444` → host services on `10.200.0.2` (dashboard/registration → `:8080`, assistant gRPC → `:8090`, etc.). Live rules: `/dev/shm/xray_config.json` only.
124|
125|## Attachment modes (summary)
126|
127|| Pattern | Used by (live) |
128|| --- | --- |
129|| Bridged NIC on `ovsbr0` | `xray` only |
130|| Shared UDS `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` | bridge + CT mounts (`assistant`, `qdrant`) |
131|| Incus `proxy` TCP | `mail-3tched`, `netmaker`, `qdrant`, `cozo` |
132|| Mesh `tcpfwd.py` (`fwd-*`) | side channels into xray/host |
133|| Host UDS `/run/opdbus/grpc.sock` | host gRPC clients, session bus |
134|
135|## Do / don't
136|
137|- **Do** check `sudo incus config device show <name>` before assuming UDS-only or proxy-only.
138|- **Do** keep mesh routes on `3tched`; strip accidental `100.69.0.0/16` via `ovsbr0`.
139|- **Do** treat the [Netmaker ACL helper](host-socket-topology-live.md#break-glass-netmaker-acl-recovery) as break-glass recovery; it enables wildcard all-node traffic and bypasses the normal D-Bus path.
140|- **Do not** put `10.200.0.1` on the host.
141|- **Do not** point live xray at `/etc/xray/config.json`.
142|- **Do not** expose Prometheus/Grafana from the netmaker container until the live topology doc is current and the path (mesh vs SNI vs loopback) is chosen.

69|pub fn valid_event_hash(hash: &str) -> bool {
70|    // ChainEvent::compute_hash delegates to event_chain::compute_hash, whose
71|    // persisted wire format is lowercase hexadecimal MD5 (32 characters).
72|    // This is an audit locator, not a plugin's BLAKE3 schema/content hash.
73|    hash.len() == 32
74|        && hash
75|            .bytes()
76|            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&byte))
77|}

94|            operation.to_string() == self.operation_id,
95|            "noncanonical operation id"

{"content":"1|#!/bin/sh
2|# build-golden.sh — prepare the golden btrfs subvolume from one release build.
3|#
4|# Populate the `golden` btrfs subvolume with the complete deployable content.
5|# Taking a read-only snapshot, transferring it with `btrfs send/receive`, and
6|# activating the received filesystem belong to the deployment process. This
7|# preparation script performs none of those deployment steps and never writes
8|# into the running host's installation or restarts a service.
9|#
10|# Layout created under $OPDBUS_ROOT (default /opt/op-dbus):
11|#
12|#   golden/                      the deployable subvolume
13|#     bin/                       release binaries
14|#     libexec/3tched/             application-only helpers
15|#     usr/bin/threetched          pinned threetched dependency
16|#     usr/share/op-dbus/          immutable config, catalog and provenance
17|#     usr/local/share/op-dbus/dashboard/  pinned production UI assets at root
18|#     sv/<service>/run            enabled application runit definitions
19|#     opt/                       immutable broker and provider runtimes
20|# Host secrets, grants, network/bootstrap services and writable data are excluded.
21|#     MANIFEST                   commit, build time, sha256 per binary
22|#
23|# Usage:
24|#   build-golden.sh                 # prepare and validate golden (default)
25|#   build-golden.sh --golden-only   # compatibility alias for the default
26|#   build-golden.sh --dry-run
27|#
28|# Retired options `--live-only` and `--no-restart` fail explicitly. Requires
29|# root to populate the btrfs subvolume. Never builds: run
30|# `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release` first (the
31|# vendored RocksDB in cozorocks needs that flag on modern GCC).
32|# `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE` may name an isolated prepared catalog; it
33|# defaults to `/var/lib/opdbus/plugin-blobs` and is never modified here.
34|# `OP_RELEASE_DIR` selects the same prepared optimized artifact directory as
35|# activate-golden.sh; it defaults to the workspace's target/release.
36|set -eu
37|
38|OPDBUS_ROOT=${OPDBUS_ROOT:-/opt/op-dbus}
39|OPDBUS_ROOT=$(realpath -e -- "$OPDBUS_ROOT")
40|GOLDEN_DIR="$OPDBUS_ROOT/golden"
41|
42|DRY_RUN=0
43|
44|SCRIPT_PATH=$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$0")
45|# Internal helper of ./activate-golden.sh; every relative input lives in deploy/runit.
46|SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$SCRIPT_PATH")/../../runit" && pwd)
47|if [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../Cargo.toml" ]; then
48|    PROJECT_ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
49|else
50|    PROJECT_ROOT=${OP_DBUS_ROOT:-$(pwd)}
51|fi
52|RELEASE_DIR=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_RELEASE_DIR:-"$PROJECT_ROOT/target/release"}")
53|MCP_AUDIENCE_POLICY_SOURCE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../config/mcp-audience-policy.json"
54|HOST_RUNTIME_PACKAGES_SOURCE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../config/host-runtime-packages.txt"
55|PERSISTED_CATALOG_DIR=${OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE:-/var/lib/opdbus/plugin-blobs}
56|PERSISTED_CATALOG_DIR=$(realpath -e -- "$PERSISTED_CATALOG_DIR")
57|case "$PERSISTED_CATALOG_DIR" in
58|    "$GOLDEN_DIR"|"$GOLDEN_DIR"/*)
59|        printf '%s\n' "catalog source must be outside the golden preparation tree" >&2
60|        exit 1
61|        ;;
62|esac
63|RETIRED_SERVICES_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/retired-services"
64|RETIRED_BINARIES_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/retired-binaries"
65|EMQX_VERSION_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../config/emqx.version"
66|EMQX_CONFIG_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/../emqx"
67|EMQX_ARTIFACT_CACHE_DIR=${EMQX_ARTIFACT_CACHE_DIR:-/var/cache/op-dbus/source-artifacts}
68|MCP_PROVIDER_ARTIFACT_CACHE_DIR=${MCP_PROVIDER_ARTIFACT_CACHE_DIR:-/var/cache/op-dbus/source-artifacts}
69|NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_VERSION_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../config/notebooklm-mcp.version"
70|EXECUTION_PYTHON_LOCK="$SCRIPT_DIR/../config/execution-python-requirements.lock"
71|EXECUTION_PYTHON_PREPARE="$SCRIPT_DIR/prepare-execution-python.sh"
72|NLM_CLI_ROOT=/opt/opdbus
73|TCHED_ROUTER_SOURCE_PIN="$PROJECT_ROOT/vendor/tched-router/source.pin"
74|TCHED_ROUTER_VENDORED_SOURCE="$PROJECT_ROOT/vendor/tched-router/source.tar.gz"
75|TCHED_ROUTER_ARTIFACT_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/target/threetched-artifacts/tched-router"
76|THREETCHED_BIN="$TCHED_ROUTER_ARTIFACT_DIR/threetched"

84|TCHED_ROUTER_BOOTSTRAP_SKILLS="$SCRIPT_DIR/../config/threetched-skills/default"
85|AGENT_BUNDLE_SOURCE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../config/agents"

87|UI_SOURCE_PIN="$UI_SOURCE_DIR/source.pin"

89|UI_SOURCE_MANIFEST="$UI_SOURCE_DIR/source-sha256sums"

98|        grep -Ev '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$SCRIPT_DIR/enabled-services" | grep -qx "$1" &&
99|        ! is_retired_service "$1"

101|
102|# Only this already-provisioned, root-owned preparation tree may be changed.
103|# Never follow a stale destination link into host state.
104|ensure_directory() (
105|    directory=$1
106|    case "$directory" in "$GOLDEN_DIR"|"$GOLDEN_DIR"/*) ;; *) die "destination outside golden: $directory" ;; esac
107|    [ ! -L "$directory" ] || die "symlink directory in golden: $directory"
108|    if [ "$directory" != "$GOLDEN_DIR" ]; then
109|        ensure_directory "$(dirname "$directory")"
110|    fi
111|    if [ ! -e "$directory" ]; then
112|        run install -d -m 0755 -o root -g root "$directory"
113|    else
114|        [ -d "$directory" ] || die "not a directory: $directory"
115|        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$directory")" = 0:0 ] || die "non-root staging directory: $directory"
116|        [ "$directory" = "$GOLDEN_DIR" ] || {
117|            [ "$(stat -c %a "$directory")" = 755 ] || run chmod 0755 "$directory"
118|        }
119|    fi
120|)
121|
122|remove_owned() (
123|    destination=$1
124|    parent=$(dirname "$destination")
125|    while [ "$parent" != "$GOLDEN_DIR" ]; do
126|        case "$parent" in "$GOLDEN_DIR"/*) ;; *) die "removal outside golden: $destination" ;; esac
127|        [ ! -L "$parent" ] || die "symlink parent in golden: $parent"
128|        parent=$(dirname "$parent")
129|    done
130|    run rm -r -- "$destination"
131|)
132|
133|# Equal bytes retain the inode and extents; metadata-only changes do not copy.
134|install_file() (
135|    mode=$1 source=$2 destination=$3
136|    ensure_directory "$(dirname "$destination")"

{"content":"1|# Local release activation
2|
3|The current native release controller prepares golden, transfers a read-only
4|snapshot with `btrfs send/receive`, and rotates read-only overlays directly at
5|the inventory's owned host targets. It retains active and previous slots.
6|The older per-file/current-symlink procedures below are historical, not an
7|alternative activation path.
8|
9|## Paths and ownership
10|
11|| Path | Purpose |
12||---|---|
13|| `/opt/op-dbus/golden` | Writable preparation subvolume; never an execution target |
14|| `/opt/op-dbus/release-send/<release-id>` | Immutable source generation used by the native transfer |
15|| Native filesystem roots `@release-a` / `@release-b` | Controller-owned received slots; never populate or select manually |
16|| Inventory-declared host targets | Read-only overlays selected by the activation transaction |
17|| `/var/lib/opdbus-release` | Protected controller state, transaction recovery and first-activation preservation |
18|
19|Retention is configurable per storage owner; there is no global five-subvolume
20|cap. Budget free bytes for preparation, send/receive and a recovery reserve
21|before starting writes. Count paths under the release root explicitly: `btrfs
22|subvolume list -o` on an ordinary directory lists descendants of its
23|containing subvolume, including unrelated Incus storage. Existing unrelated
24|subvolumes are not permission to delete storage. Preserve the category,
25|timing, vector and state subvolumes owned by cache/Snowball. Retain the previous active
26|release for rollback; retire only explicitly identified obsolete releases.
27|
28|## Current entry point and base prerequisites
29|
30|Run `sudo ./activate-golden.sh` from the repository root, preserving the
31|explicit prepared-artifact selectors described below. It validates the
32|independent root-owned release kit, provisions/reconciles slots, prepares
33|golden, then invokes native release/activation. It does not compile or reseal.
34|Use `/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch status` for the
35|authoritative slot, journal, overlay and readiness receipt; `rollback` selects
36|the compatible previous release through the same controller.
37|
38|Independent base prerequisites must be ready before the application cutover:
39|
40|- `identity-roots` restores only existing identity-root inventory. An empty
41|  inventory succeeds without provisioning; any failed restoration fails the
42|  service. Login/start/stop never add or remove Btrfs members. Its readiness
43|  marker is emitted only after successful restoration.
44|- On the restored host, the native Open vSwitch package owns its daemons.
45|  The runit `ovsdb-server` service observes the validated native PID with
46|  procps `pidwait`; its bounded check queries the actual Unix socket for
47|  `Open_vSwitch`. It must not launch duplicate daemons, change topology, or
48|  run the old uplink/bootstrap chain. Inspect sockets with native metadata
49|  and protocol tools; a generic directory listing can omit them.
50|- Independent `op-warp-endpoint` restores only the existing declared local
51|  endpoint from `/etc/op-dbus/warp-ssh.json`; `endpoint.sh check` verifies
52|  ownership, address/peer, aliases and MTU. An UP persistent TUN with
53|  NO-CARRIER is not evidence of SSH, remote ingress or authenticated access.
54|  This service does not restore MASQUE, firewall or policy-routing state.
55|- Logger definitions require the existing system `svlog` account/group and
56|  appropriately owned log directories. Long-lived helper services use the
57|  available `sleep infinity`, not an assumed `pause` executable.
58|
59|Runtime TLS, protected capability/toolset policy, provider keys and the
60|production router's matching configuration/token state remain outside the
61|release. The runtime MCP audience and toolset JSON files must be root-owned
62|mode 0600; the bridge rejects group/world-readable policy before binding.
63|Restore missing inputs only from a verified authoritative backup,
64|without printing secret values, overwriting present state, substituting
65|template grants or minting replacement identities. A router token must match
66|the same production gateway's persisted token hash; an unrelated historical
67|configuration is not recovery proof.
68|
69|On this host, `op-storage` and `op-storage-kernel-guard` remain persistently
70|OFF until explicit owner reauthorization. Activation is not permission to
71|rearm them. Enable the independent early-boot release hook only after a
72|successful activation receipt; do not reboot as a deployment check. A
73|received inactive slot is not a deployed application or a mounted 3tchedFS.
74|
75|
76|## Prepare
77|
78|Build the native glibc workspace, prepare its pinned UI and threetched
79|artifacts, and explicitly seal/persist with the freshly built `opblob` and
80|the service's schema-shaping environment. Preserve the previous catalogs and
81|review additions/removals before a live reseal. `build-golden.sh` accepts
82|`OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE` for isolated release preparation.
83|
84|Reuse already-built native binaries by setting `OP_RELEASE_DIR` to the complete
85|prepared executable directory; the default is `target/release`. Set
86|`EMQX_ARTIFACT_CACHE_DIR` and `MCP_PROVIDER_ARTIFACT_CACHE_DIR` when the pinned
87|EMQX archive and nlm wheel are cached outside `/var/cache/op-dbus/source-artifacts`.
88|These selectors do not rebuild binaries or weaken artifact digest checks.
89|The pinned EMQX archive is still digest-verified before extraction. Its unused
90|esockd demonstration private key is excluded from the prepared payload;
91|configured runtime TLS keys remain outside the release at `/etc/emqx/certs`.
92|
93|The execution payload requires GNU Python 3.14. When the host default differs,
94|`OP_EXECUTION_PYTHON_BUNDLE` may name an existing standalone native runtime
95|directory. Preparation copies that runtime into the execution payload, verifies
96|its relocated base prefix, and installs the hash-locked tools into that private
97|prefix. The received release therefore does not depend on a user-managed
98|interpreter under `/home`; the host's default Python is unchanged. Without this
99|selector, preparation retains the native-host virtual-environment path.
100|The preparation receipt records the runtime binary and preparer digests, so a
101|changed interpreter or preparation implementation invalidates reuse.
102|
103|Golden preparation generates the restart inventory from the prepared bytes.
104|Shell assignments are not executable names; quoted substitutions, continuations,
105|declared function arguments and attached redirection paths retain their
106|dependencies without executing the scripts. Captured-source and versioned
107|skill-packaging provenance are classified by their complete JSON structure,
108|not by filename. Unknown executable/configuration references, mixed provenance
109|and configuration records, and absent release inputs still stop preparation.
110|An inventory-helper repair can be built and selected independently; it does
111|not require replacing the existing application binaries or their catalog.
112|
113|When a plugin version changes, rebuild `op-grpc-bridge` from the same plugin
114|source as `opblob` and activate that bridge with the matching catalog. The
115|bridge compares each sealed plugin version and method declaration with its
116|compiled compatibility contract before dispatch. Building only the sealer,
117|even for a description-only version change, leaves the old bridge rejecting
118|calls. Catalog parity and bridge readiness alone do not verify this boundary.
119|
120|Before the workspace build and sealing, select the prepared threetched binary
121|with the paired absolute `THREETCHED_CAPTURE_BIN` and
122|`THREETCHED_CAPTURE_MANIFEST` paths. Keep those selectors identical across both
123|steps; without them discovery uses the installed binary, which may belong to
124|the previous release. The runtime selectors remain `/usr/bin/threetched` and
125|`/usr/share/op-dbus/threetched-manifests/tched-router.json`. Follow the
126|[binary feature preparation procedure](../../../crates/threetched-fs/README.md#add-a-threetched-feature-from-the-binary)
127|for the exact environment, isolated `opblob seal-plugins` invocation, catalog
128|review and mounted verification. Golden preparation rejects mismatched sealed
129|binary or manifest digests.
130|
131|### Separate host filesystem surfaces
132|
133|Our filesystem executable is `3tched-fs` (Cargo package `tched-fs`, retained
134|source directory `crates/threetched-fs`). Its plugin is `tched_fs`, displayed
135|as 3tchedFS. The external ZeroClaw-derived executable remains `threetched`.
136|The host projects two disjoint views of the same sealed catalog:
137|
138|| Mount | Projected plugins |
139|| --- | --- |
140|| `/run/mounts/3tchedFS` | OP-DBUS plugins, including `tched_fs`, excluding the four below |
141|| `/run/mounts/threetched` | `threetched`, `tched_router`, `tched_plugins`, `tched_skills` |
142|
143|Both use our FUSE engine and kernel subtype `fuse.3tchedFS`; their kernel
144|source labels distinguish `3tchedFS` and `threetched`. Filtering changes only
145|the view: the catalog pin, per-plugin schema hashes and operation admission
146|remain authoritative. A mounted schema does not prove session provisioning
147|or permission to execute an operation.
148|
149|`deploy/host-fuse/3tchedfs.fstab` declares the two mounts. The release carries
150|`mount-3tchedfs` under `/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers`; the host's
151|`/usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS` and `/etc/rcS.d/S13op-3tchedfs-mount` link to
152|that adapter. Explicit late mounting after `S12op-release-activate` is why
153|the entries use `noauto`. The old `threetched-fs` runit service is retired.
154|The adapter uses the existing root-owned mode-0400 or mode-0600
155|`/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session` and `human-lungs-call-owner-uid` selection
156|files; it never mints an identity or grants access.
157|
158|After a catalog-changing activation, unmount the old host views normally,
159|then mount each declared fstab target to capture the new release's catalog.
160|Preserve any outstanding operation receipts before unmounting. Boot wiring
161|and live mount readiness are separate from a reboot verification.
162|The host's fstab entries and helper/boot symlinks live outside the application
163|snapshot. Rolling back to a release that predates the two-view adapter also
164|requires restoring the saved host mount configuration; application rollback
165|does not undo those host files.
166|
167|After extracting deterministic UI assets into the prepared tree, set
168|`dashboard/index.html` to the preparation timestamp before taking the read-only
169|snapshot. Archive timestamps are epoch-based; preserving them on this HTTP
170|entry point can cause a browser's old `If-Modified-Since` request to receive
171|304 and retain an obsolete bundle. Keep the archive and content hashes intact,
172|and verify an old conditional request returns 200 after activation.
173|
174|For the first clean baseline, move the previous golden contents into an
175|ordinary recovery directory before repopulating the existing golden
176|subvolume. This prevents untracked legacy binaries, provider trees and
177|container files from becoming release inputs. Do not move nested subvolumes
178|or the golden subvolume itself. The intentionally staged `bin/nlm` wrapper
179|is additional to the Cargo binaries and must remain.
180|
181|Resolve target secrets and the threetched router before activating the bridge.
182|The `tched-router` service uses the pinned `/usr/bin/threetched` executable,
183|loopback port 8084 and private mutable configuration. Its authenticated
184|generation credential must be issued by that same gateway and persisted
185|with its corresponding threetched token hash. A token from a temporary gateway
186|is not valid for the production gateway. This threetched backend provisioning
187|does not introduce OP-DBUS UI pairing.
188|
189|Task elevation uses the static PAM service file `deploy/pam/op-dbus-elevate`,
190|staged into the release and activated as `/etc/pam.d/op-dbus-elevate`. For
191|each exact task, the authenticated caller authorizes the request by entering
192|the root account password; PAM checks that password and account validity.
193|The existing verified caller-principal and capability-grant checks remain
194|in force, and the resulting one-use authorization ticket is bound to that
195|principal, session, plugin, method and arguments. The workflow has no
196|per-principal Unix-user map prerequisite.
197|
198|Control Plane inherits its provider from the threetched `control_plane` agent.
199|Set the public service variable `TCHED_ROUTER_CONTROL_PLANE_MODEL_PROVIDER`

Audit complete. The script is not working end-to-end against the current deployment.

Main findings:

1. D-Bus-first is not consistently followed.
   Direct Incus creation/start and device changes bypass existing plugin admission and authoritative state publication.
   provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:239–244
   bind-instance-root.sh:66–74
   External disk/leaf preparation remains legitimate host maintenance; not every operation has a suitable plugin equivalent.

2. Host paths are stale.
   Both adoption paths reference absent executables or /run/mount/3tchedFS. The verified host paths are /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs and /run/mounts/3tchedFS.
   provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:290,324
   prepare-chatbot-adoption.sh:26–29

3. The legacy wrapper uses a removed receipt interface.
   It reads sibling result/error files, but current FUSE returns the receipt on the same open call descriptor. Fixing paths alone will not fix this.
   provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:331–343

4. Its adoption plan is rejected by the owner.
   The wrapper emits principal_group, which CleanPlan rejects as an unknown field—after native/storage preparation.
   provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:464
   crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/identity_clean_provision.rs:52–77

5. Root binding deletes the guest FUSE mount declaration.
   Replacing /etc/fstab removes the entry required by the guest mount service.
   bind-instance-root.sh:76–78

6. Ordinary upgrade sync leaves the root detached.
   It unmounts the container’s root and layers, but reconstructs them only in boot mode, then reports success.
   sync-instance-upgrade.sh:88–109,135–162

7. Grant publication is unsafe and happens too late.
   The guest can already be running and boot-enabled before grants are checked. An undefined selected group can invalidate the entire grant document; concurrent policy changes can also be overwritten.
   provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:503–548
